sections.text:
1 Hic liber ex reliquiis duorum codicum consarcinatus est : 1o Ff. 1-53, codex ab
Eleutherio exaratus, nunc initio mutilus, fere totus impletur excerptis ex syntag-
mate quod dicitur Laurentiano (cf. Fr. Boll, Sitzungsb. bayer. Akad., 1899, p. 88 s.).
— 2o Ff. 54-73, codex fortasse eadem manu certe saec. XIV descriptus item excerpta
ex syntagmate astrologico continet, nempe ex illis collectaneis saec. XI e quibus
Marciani 334, 335 et Parisinus 2506 fluxerunt (cf. Catal. Venet., p. 37, n. 1). Multo
pleniorem olim fuisse librum Taurinensem numeri capitulorum monstrant rubro
pigmento in margine adscripti, qui passim supersunt, sed plerumque a bibliopega
abscissi sunt. Multa folia interciderunt, multa iam legi non possunt, itaque mihi
ignoscatur si in recensendo opere titulum aliquem praetermiserim.
sections.en: 1 This book was patched together from the remains of two codices: 1st Ff. 1-53, a codex written out by Eleutherios, now mutilated at the beginning, is almost entirely filled with excerpts from the syntagma which is called Laurentian (cf. Fr. Boll, Sitzungsb. bayer. Akad., 1899, p. 88 f.). — 2nd Ff. 54-73, a codex perhaps by the same hand, certainly copied in the 14th century, likewise contains excerpts from an astrological syntagma, namely from those 11th-century collections from which Marciani 334, 335 and Parisinus 2506 flowed (cf. Catal. Venet., p. 37, n. 1). The numbers of the chapters written in red pigment in the margin, which survive here and there but have mostly been cut off by the binder, show that the Turin book was once much fuller. Many leaves have fallen out, many can no longer be read, and so let me be forgiven if in reviewing the work I have passed over some title.

summary.headline: Turin Codex C Contents
summary.text: Description of Codex C, VII, 10 (B, VI, 12), a 14th-century Turin astrological manuscript partly copied in 1389 by Eleutherios of Mytilene, followed by its contents: solar and lunar cycles, Easter calculation, epacts, lunar cycles, psalmic lots, lunar calculations, earthquake theory, and astrological excerpts from Paul explained by Heliodorus.
